ambiguities.evidence: The sentence after Equations (2.14)-(2.16) says only that C, c > 0 are absolute constants (PDF page 16; printed page 27).
ambiguities.impact: A faithful standalone formalization may existentially quantify a universal C or select a proved universal value, but it may not treat C as depending on X or lambda.
ambiguities.issue: The source does not give a numerical value for C.

ambiguities.evidence: The same symbol C occurs in Equation (2.15), Equation (2.16), and nearby prose, followed by the collective statement that C and c are absolute constants (PDF page 16; printed page 27).
ambiguities.impact: For Equation (2.16) alone, only existence of a suitable universal positive constant is fixed; coupling it numerically to constants in other displayed bounds is not determined by this passage.
ambiguities.issue: The typography reuses C in nearby bounds without explicitly stating whether every occurrence denotes one common numerical constant or conventional possibly enlarged absolute constants.

contract_plain_english: There is a universal positive constant C such that every mean-zero sub-gaussian random variable X has its moment generating function bounded, for every real lambda, by exp(C times lambda squared times the square of X's psi_2 norm). The source leaves the numerical value of C unspecified.

source_evidence.observation: For a sub-gaussian random variable X with E X = 0, the source states E exp(lambda X) <= exp(C lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2) for every lambda in R.

source_evidence.anchor: Sentence immediately following Equations (2.14)-(2.16): Here C, c > 0 are absolute constants
source_evidence.observation: The coefficient C in Equation (2.16) is positive and absolute, hence independent of X and lambda; no numerical value is specified.
The norm in Equation (2.16) is the sub-gaussian norm ||X||_{psi_2} = inf {t > 0 : E exp(X^2/t^2) <= 2}.

Under E X = 0, Proposition 2.5.2 adds the equivalent MGF property: there exists K5 > 0 such that E exp(lambda X) <= exp(K5^2 lambda^2) for all lambda in R; the equivalence parameters differ by at most an absolute constant factor.

binders: C > 0: an absolute constant, supplied universally and independently of X and lambda.
X: a sub-gaussian random variable, universally quantified.
lambda in R, universally quantified after X.
conclusions: There is an absolute constant C > 0 such that, for every centered sub-gaussian random variable X and every lambda in R, E exp(lambda X) <= exp(C lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2).
definitions_and_conventions: E exp(lambda X) is the moment generating function of X evaluated at the real parameter lambda.
An absolute constant is independent of the particular random variable X and of lambda.
The source writes C lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2 in the exponent, not C^2 lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2.
implicit_context: Equation (2.16) is one of the bounds obtained by restating Proposition 2.5.2 in terms of the sub-gaussian norm.
The underlying probability space and the standard measurability conventions carried by the term random variable remain implicit.
The same surrounding list also uses symbols C and c for absolute constants, but Equation (2.16) depends only on C.

details: C is universal rather than chosen separately for each X or lambda.
After fixing a centered sub-gaussian X, the inequality holds for all real lambda.
The mean-zero condition E X = 0 is an explicit antecedent of Equation (2.16).
The source does not replace X by X - E X inside the MGF; it assumes X itself is centered.
The exponent is quadratic in both lambda and ||X||_{psi_2}.
The same X appears in the MGF, in the mean-zero hypothesis, and in the psi_2 norm.
The relation is the non-strict upper bound <=.
C is positive and absolute but its numerical value is not fixed by the cited passage.

undebatable_constraints: The claim applies only under the explicit centering hypothesis E X = 0.
The MGF inequality must hold for every lambda in R, including both signs and lambda = 0.
The left-hand side is E exp(lambda X), not E exp(lambda^2 X^2) and not the MGF of a separately centered transform.
The right-hand exponent has the form C lambda^2 ||X||_{psi_2}^2.
C must be a positive absolute constant independent of X and lambda.
The inequality is non-strict and points from the MGF to its exponential upper bound.
The psi_2 norm is the threshold-2 exponential-square norm of Definition 2.5.6.
